SECTION 1
* This is point 1. The writer, a 24-year-old, feels frustrated because older people criticize him for spending money on things like holidays and meals, instead of saving every penny to buy a home.
* This is point 2. It’s very hard for young people to buy a house because house prices are high, homes are in short supply, and banks are not lending easily, making home ownership feel out of reach.
* This is point 3. The writer thinks many young people will never own homes and will spend their lives paying rent to landlords who then judge them for not saving enough.
* This is point 4. Unlike older workers, young people under 25 don’t get the full “national living wage” and may earn as little as £7.05 or even £5.60 per hour, even when working the same jobs and hours.
* This is point 5. Many young workers earn very low annual incomes—possibly as little as £14,500—and are more likely to have unstable zero-hours contracts with no guaranteed work hours.
